issues.legal_issue: Proceedings to determine whether a person and their property are evacuee property cannot continue to a posthumous declaration when the person dies before the declaration and the property has devolved to heirs by succession.
material_facts: Proceedings to determine the person’s status and the status of their property began while the person was alive.
An appeal seeking a declaration that the person and their property were evacuee was pending when the person died, before the appellate authority made that declaration.
The property devolved on the heirs in specific shares by succession under Mohammedan law, rather than by transfer from the deceased.
The governing scheme contained no provision for substituting the heirs or continuing the proceedings against them after the person’s death.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings lapsed on the person’s death. The appellate authority had no jurisdiction to declare the deceased an evacuee or the property that had devolved on the heirs to be evacuee property, and its declaration was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(d) and 2(f), the definitions of evacuee and evacuee property concern a person with a right or interest in the property; section 7 requires notice and an inquiry before property may be declared evacuee property, and section 8 provides for vesting following that declaration. Read together with rule 6 and its notice form, these provisions contemplate proceedings against a living person. A declaration cannot operate retrospectively to displace property that has already devolved on heirs by operation of law. Succession is not a transfer within section 2(f)(1), and the restriction on transfers in section 40 does not alter devolution by death. Section 43 addresses death after vesting and does not authorize a declaration after death. Section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply to the Custodian, and section 45 applies the Code only for specified purposes, not substitution; unlike section 93 of the Presidency Towns Insolvency Act and section 17 of the Provincial Insolvency Act, the governing scheme has no provision for continuation after death. The earlier decision in Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Custodian General of Evacuee Property decided only that the informant could appeal and left this jurisdictional question open.

rule.if: evacuee_property_status_appeal and person_died_before_declaration and property_devolved_to_heirs_by_succession and no_post_death_continuation_procedure

predicates.evacuee_property_status_appeal: An appeal is pending to determine whether a person and their property have the relevant evacuee status.
predicates.person_died_before_declaration: The person whose status is being determined dies before the authority declares that person or the property to have that status.
predicates.property_devolved_to_heirs_by_succession: The property passes to the person’s heirs by succession upon death, rather than by a transfer from the deceased.
predicates.no_post_death_continuation_procedure: The governing scheme provides no procedure to substitute heirs or continue the status proceedings after the person dies.

issues.definition: When an appeal over evacuee status is pending, the person dies before a declaration, the property has passed to heirs by succession, and there is no procedure for continuing the case after death, the proceedings lapse and a posthumous declaration is invalid.
